data.name: Abraham
data.long_meaning: Abraham is a revered prophetic name meaning 'Father of Multitudes' or 'Exalted Father'. Derived from the Hebrew 'Avraham', he is regarded as the founding patriarch of monotheism in Islam, Christianity, and Judaism. His unwavering devotion to God, exemplified through trials and divine covenants, makes Abraham a name symbolizing faith, leadership, and divine blessing.
data.spiritual_meaning: Abraham symbolizes complete submission to God, spiritual legacy, and unwavering belief in divine guidance. His story marks the beginning of monotheistic revelation and righteous lineage.
data.numerology_meaning: Number 1 reflects leadership, independence, and originality. It matches Abraham's nature as a spiritual pioneer and foundation-builder of divine faith.

data.cultural_impact: Abraham is a widely recognized name in the Abrahamic religions, indicated by his inclusion in monotheistic traditions such as Christianity, Judaism, and Islam. He is known for his crucial role in the development of monotheism, as well as his notable contributions to religious scriptures and beliefs. Abraham's life story has inspired numerous works of art, literature, and scholarly studies, cementing its significant impact on global culture.
data.spiritual_significance: Abraham is considered a righteous and obedient prophet in Islamic, Jewish, and Christian belief. His profound faith in God, demonstrated through his willingness to sacrifice his son Ishmael or Isaac (depending on the tradition), illustrates unwavering devotion and trust. The trials Abraham faced, including separation from his father's idolatrous ways and his belief in the unity of God, set an example for future generations. A paradigm of faith, his name continues to serve as an inspiration for spiritual growth and connection with the Divine.
